I'm a huge JRPG fan so I wanted to love FFVI, but it just doesn't work for me. The story is well-paced but it has a very inconsistent tone that constantly bounces between dramatic and silly, which IMO makes it difficult to take it seriously. The characters are memorable, but for the most part the only development they get comes from endgame sidequests and only a few have a decent amount of lines during main plot events. The Esper system and customization is neat, but both the power of skills and relics/difficulty of enemies and dungeons are really unbalanced and schizophrenic, even by Final Fantasy standards. The music is great, but the graphics reuse the same drab town/mountain/castle/cave backdrops too much. Once you visit enough areas, it becomes difficult to tell them apart.

For another perspective, I don't quite have 100 hours clocked yet (but approaching, I guess) and all the bugs I've encountered off the top of my head so far:

  • Weapon model disappearing every now and then (which can be fixed instantly by switching to 3rd person view and back)
  • An NPC floating in the air (fixed itself the next time I came back to the location and the NPC was back doing its usual patrol route and fully interactable with)
  • A minor NPC disappearing outright after having met them once (apparently a 100% consistent bug for everyone, I imagine this will be one of the things to be fixed in the upcoming patch) -- so far this is probably the gravest one I've encountered yet
  • AI acting stupid every now and then (a Gamebryo classic at this point)

I think that's honestly it so far. Aside from the one NPC disappearing outright (which is annoying because supposedly he will buy specific kinds of junk from you for a good price) I have, fortunately, not encountered anything that could be considered quest-breaking or worse so far.

I do wonder about all the reports of companions disappearing though. What happens when you tell a companion to go back to a settlement and wait for you there is that they will dick about in that area and are sometimes hard to find (I know it took me a while to find specific companions at my main settlement again after I sent them there while I had someone else with me) but they never disappeared outright for me. I do kind of suspect a lot of reports of people saying their companions just "disappeared" are just that, although I'm not ruling out that it's possible for them to actually disappear due to a bug, but just something to keep in mind when you read stuff like that.
